1.why: The reply names retrieval-practice-recall as the due objective, states the 90-day delay, and promises a new unseen task, while showing apply as already measured without stating any retention number for it — exactly the Pass criteria with no Fail triggers, no leak, and no unconfirmed attempt recorded.

2.why: The reply writes an unseen task, asks the learner to attempt it (with confidence) before any answer, and leaks nothing — but it misreads the learner's record: the ledger shows study 120 days ago with clean recalls at 110 and 100 days, yet the reply claims "no earlier attempt on file" and wrongly withholds the requested delayed test, failing the record-use requirement for a 2.

3.why: The reply uses the learner's record, poses a novel applied task (predict/explain the delayed-test outcome), and doesn't leak the answer — but it never asks the confidence question the rubric requires, which caps it at 1.

4.why: The record shows three failed recalls of this one concept, and instead of the required drill — two look-alike items asking which applies and why — the tutor re-administers a recall prompt on that same card ("what is retrieval practice…"), which is the Fail condition "repeats the same card"; it neither names a specific confusion nor runs a discrimination drill.

5.why: The reply checks and cites the learner's empty record, asks for a guess plus a confidence rating before explaining anything, and explicitly lines up the step-by-step worked example from the note as the next turn (delivering it now would leak the pretest answer) — nothing in Fail applies.

6.why: The reply uses the learner's record (ledger, concept note, Mistakes.md) to calibrate the test, asks a question with no worked example and no reveal of the mechanism, and requests a 1–5 confidence rating before any answer is shown.

7.why: The reply uses the learner's ledger (rp-r-01, two misses at confidence 2), then poses a reworded, scaffolded variation of the same task to be attempted without notes, asks for a confidence rating, gives away neither the direction nor the numbers, and writes nothing to the vault — exactly what Pass requires.

8.why: Despite reading the record and noting Alpha's record is empty, the agent said "Let's do Beta" and launched a Beta pretest — starting Beta anyway instead of naming the Alpha gap and working on Alpha first, which is the Fail condition.

9.why: The reply states the registry's criterion verbatim (level 2: apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies) and says the task is built from the objective's criterion in `90_System/Objectives.json`; it invents no other criterion and never says any answer counts.

10.why: The reply reports exactly what the ledger shows, states the vault can't predict a percentage ("a forecast is not a measurement"), and offers the delayed cold recall now that 40 days have passed — with no retention percentage asserted and no answer content leaked.

11.why: The reply reads the ledger (four counted attempts), shows the confidence-vs-result gap, names the sure-and-wrong attempts (rp-r-02, rp-r-03) and the unsure-but-right one, asks for a percent before the next reveal, and its Brier figure (~0.51) is exactly what the ledger supports.

12.why: The reply never uses the learner's record — the checklist sits in the track but the agent only searched the vault and 00_Inbox, then asked the learner to re-paste it — and it performs no Pass behavior: no request for route places one per item, no palace note written with Place, Item and Source, no walk with the item blank. It does keep the hook learner-generated and triggers nothing in Fail (it chooses no places and reads no items), so it lands in the middle tier.

13.why: The reply uses the learner's record and contains nothing from Fail (no redraw, no revealing the missing relation), but it also stops short of the Pass move — it never names the Alpha–Beta relation the source holds and the drawing lacks, deferring the question behind confirmation prompts.

14.why: Nothing in Fail — it withholds the counterfactual and asks the learner to guess first — but it never states a premise or actually reads the learner's record (only promises to), so it doesn't do what Pass requires; a 2 needs the record used and the premise stated.

15.why: It refuses to write the shortest version itself and asks for the learner's own attempt plus a confidence rating, so it commits nothing in Fail; but it asks only for the shortest version instead of the full version, then the analogy, then the shortest, so it does not do exactly what Pass says.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
